sections.h2: What Creekside at Flintrock West homes are like
paragraphs: Where the East section sits along Stephanie Ln, the West section runs along Kaden Way. It is a small gated pocket of Flintrock, and the setting feels like the rest of The Hills, with rolling ground, mature oaks and cedars, and views over open land and golf. Homes here are priced from about $1.2M to $2M, so you are looking at larger, well finished houses with plenty of glass.

The Flintrock HOA covers the section, and entry is through the gates. Because the landscape blends into The Hills, the tree cover is thicker than in some newer parts of Flintrock. That shade is pleasant in July, and it also means a steady drip of leaves, pollen, webs and bird droppings on the windows.

sections.h2: What Creekside at Flintrock West windows deal with
paragraphs: Shaded glass collects different grime than sunny glass. Oak pollen sticks to damp panes in March and April, cedar pollen follows from December to February, and spider webs build in the eaves and window frames all year. Leaves and seed pods settle into screens and tracks, which can leave a dark line along the bottom edge of the glass. Irrigation is the other regular issue, because sprinklers throw hard water onto lower panes and leave white spots.

Our dual RO, 4 stage pure water system, with a DI resin tank, brings water down to near 0 TDS. Glass dries without spots or soap film, and the frame stays clean. Screens are $5 each, tracks are $5, and hard water spot removal is $10 per pane when deposits need more than a rinse.

sections.h2: How we work Creekside at Flintrock West
paragraphs: Gate access is arranged by text before each visit. Send the address and your gate instructions, and we will check in on arrival. We carry 200 gallons of water on our 8 ft skid, so we never use your spigot. Kaden Way is a short run, so we often group it with Stephanie Ln and nearby Flintrock streets, which keeps travel short and helps us book you within about two weeks. Tree shade also encourages algae on north facing walls, so a house soft wash from $0.20 per sq ft is a natural add on. We soft wash stucco and limestone, and we never pressure wash limestone.

We do not have a size band for this section, so for illustration, a 4,000 sq ft home would be about $400 for exterior windows at $0.10 per sq ft. Expect about 45 to 60 minutes per 1,000 sq ft, plus about 30 minutes per 1,000 sq ft for the inside. Minimum job is $200.
